title: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters
main_claim: There is a k0 such that for every k ≥ k0 the standard map f_k(x,y)=(x+y+k sin2πx, y+k sin2πx) on T^2 has positive metric entropy with respect to area. Equivalently, the top Lyapunov exponent is positive on a set of positive area. This would settle Sinai's conjecture in the Berger–Turaev formulation. The proof argues by contradiction: suppose arbitrarily large k had zero exponents. Two estimates with constants uniform in M=2πk+4 are combined with a dyadic multiscale limit-measure argument. The first is an exponential bound on near-full-rate cancellations (Thm 3.1, via a local scarcity lemma). The second is a weighted product estimate across fast bridges (Thm 5.1, via contracting Dirichlet graphs).
